anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet, the battery-feed isolation diode U7 (SS2040FL) has its anode (pin 1) tied to NET0008 and its cathode (pin 2) tied to NET0028. NET0008 is the BAT+ rail (it carries the barrel-jack center pin J3.1, USB VBUS from J10.1, and the regulator input IC2.A2/VIN), while NET0028 is the BAT- return (barrel-jack pin J3.3, per the on-sheet note '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug / 1 is center, center is positive'). Thus the diode is oriented with its anode on the positive rail and its cathode on the negative rail, i.e. forward-biased across BAT+ and BAT- rather than in series between the cell and BAT+.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the diode is a series isolation device: 'U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+ ... netlist: anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+.' The cathode must sit on the BAT+ net and the anode on the raw battery node, so the diode blocks USB/adapter back-feed into the cell without shorting the rails.

evidence.quote: Battery (U7, 18650 holder) → pin 1 → Net-(U6-A) → U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+. ... netlist: anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+
EthernetAndPower.kicad_sch: U7 'SS2040FL' pin1=NET0008, pin2=NET0028; J3 pin1(center)=NET0008, J3 pin3=NET0028; IC2 VIN=NET0008; J10 VBUS=NET0008

anomalies.impact: The isolation diode is forward-biased directly across the power rails, shorting BAT+ to BAT- through the diode (and effectively across the 18650 cell). The battery would discharge through the diode, the USB/adapter input and the regulator VIN would be shorted to the negative return, preventing normal power-up and likely causing overheating/damage; the intended back-feed blocking function is lost.

This is reported as the single anomaly with moderate confidence.
